items.q: What is FolderCast?
items.a: FolderCast is a Roku TV app that lets you browse and enjoy photos, videos, and music selected from a phone, tablet, or computer connected to the same Wi-Fi network.

items.q: How do I get started?
items.a: Open FolderCast on Roku, scan the QR code shown on your TV or enter its displayed address in a browser, choose files or folders, then browse and play them using your Roku remote.

items.q: Do I need to install a companion app on my phone or computer?
items.a: No. Use a compatible web browser on your phone, tablet, or computer. No separate companion app is required.

items.q: Do my Roku and phone or computer need to be on the same Wi-Fi?
items.a: Yes. Connect the Roku and the device sharing media to the same local Wi-Fi network. Guest networks or network isolation may prevent them from communicating.

items.q: Do I need an internet connection or a FolderCast account?
items.a: FolderCast is designed for local Wi-Fi sharing and does not require a cloud media library or a separate FolderCast account. Internet access may still be needed for Roku installation, purchases, or account services.

items.q: Can I connect by typing an address instead of scanning the QR code?
items.a: Yes. Enter the address displayed by FolderCast on your TV into a browser on your phone, tablet, or computer.

items.q: Can I share a complete folder instead of selecting files one by one?
items.a: Yes. Choose an entire media folder in the browser, or select individual supported media files.

items.q: Can I share several folders?
items.a: Yes. You can add multiple folders and individual file selections from the same connected device.

items.q: Can I connect more than one phone or computer?
items.a: Yes. FolderCast supports multiple connected devices and organizes their shared media by source device.

items.q: Can I name my connected device?
items.a: Yes. Give a connected browser device a friendly name to help identify it on your TV. The browser remembers that name locally.

items.q: What is the Selected files collection?
items.a: Files chosen individually from one browser device appear together in its Selected files collection. Additional individual selections are added to that collection.

items.q: Can I drag and drop files or folders?
items.a: Yes, on desktop browsers that support drag-and-drop selection.

items.q: What is FolderCast?
items.a: FolderCast is a Roku TV app that lets you browse and enjoy photos, videos, and music selected from a phone, tablet, or computer connected to the same Wi-Fi network.

items.q: How do I get started?
items.a: Open FolderCast on Roku, scan the QR code shown on your TV or enter its displayed address in a browser, choose files or folders, then browse and play them using your Roku remote.

items.q: Do I need to install a companion app on my phone or computer?
items.a: No. Use a compatible web browser on your phone, tablet, or computer. No separate companion app is required.

items.q: Do my Roku and phone or computer need to be on the same Wi-Fi?
items.a: Yes. Connect the Roku and the device sharing media to the same local Wi-Fi network. Guest networks or network isolation may prevent them from communicating.

items.q: Do I need an internet connection or a FolderCast account?
items.a: FolderCast is designed for local Wi-Fi sharing and does not require a cloud media library or a separate FolderCast account. Internet access may still be needed for Roku installation, purchases, or account services.

items.q: Can I connect by typing an address instead of scanning the QR code?
items.a: Yes. Enter the address displayed by FolderCast on your TV into a browser on your phone, tablet, or computer.

items.q: Can I share a complete folder instead of selecting files one by one?
items.a: Yes. Choose an entire media folder in the browser, or select individual supported media files.

items.q: Can I share several folders?
items.a: Yes. You can add multiple folders and individual file selections from the same connected device.

items.q: Can I connect more than one phone or computer?
items.a: Yes. FolderCast supports multiple connected devices and organizes their shared media by source device.

items.q: Can I name my connected device?
items.a: Yes. Give a connected browser device a friendly name to help identify it on your TV. The browser remembers that name locally.

items.q: What is the Selected files collection?
items.a: Files chosen individually from one browser device appear together in its Selected files collection. Additional individual selections are added to that collection.

items.q: Can I drag and drop files or folders?
items.a: Yes, on desktop browsers that support drag-and-drop selection.

items.q: Can I remove shared files or folders?
items.a: Yes. Remove an individual file selection or an entire shared folder from the browser sharing page. Your original files are not deleted.

items.q: Does FolderCast preserve my folder structure?
items.a: Yes. Browse shared folders and their subfolders in a TV-friendly grid, with breadcrumbs showing your current location.

items.q: How do I navigate the library?
items.a: Use the Roku remote directional buttons to move between items and OK to open them. Use Back to return to the parent folder or previous screen.

items.q: Can FolderCast browse large folders?
items.a: Yes. FolderCast supports browsing large collections and displays additional items as you navigate. Loading times can vary by device, network, and collection size.

items.q: Which photo formats are recognized?
items.a: FolderCast recognizes JPG/JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, AVIF, HEIC, and HEIF selections. Whether a photo can be displayed depends on your Roku device and the file.

items.q: Can I zoom, pan, or rotate photos?
items.a: Yes. The photo viewer includes zoom in/out, panning around enlarged images, 90-degree rotation, and multiple fit modes.

items.q: Can I move between photos without returning to the folder?
items.a: Yes. Use the Roku remote to move to the previous or next photo in the same folder.

items.q: Does FolderCast have a photo slideshow?
items.a: Yes. Start a full-screen slideshow from a photo to automatically display photos in that folder with smooth transitions.

items.q: Can I change slideshow speed or pause it?
items.a: Yes. Adjust the slide duration from 1 to 15 seconds, and press OK to pause or resume.

items.q: Which audio formats are recognized?
items.a: FolderCast recognizes MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV, FLAC, OGG, and WMA selections. Actual playback depends on the Roku device and audio encoding.

items.q: Does the music player show album artwork and song information?
items.a: Yes. It shows artwork when available, playback progress, track information, and available metadata such as genre, year, format, and bitrate.

items.q: Can I shuffle or repeat music?
items.a: Yes. The music player offers Shuffle, Repeat All, and Repeat One, along with previous/next track and 10-second skip controls.

items.q: Can I choose a song from the current folder playlist?
items.a: Yes. Open a track directly from the folder playlist in the audio player.

items.q: Which video formats are recognized?
items.a: FolderCast recognizes MP4, M4V, MOV, WebM, MKV, and AVI selections. Playback is not guaranteed for every file: Roku model, Roku OS, codecs, and the source file determine compatibility.

items.q: Can I pause, replay, or seek through a video?
items.a: Yes. The video player supports play/pause, replay, restart, 10-second forward/backward skips, and press-and-hold seeking.

items.q: Will FolderCast remember where I stopped watching?
items.a: For eligible videos, FolderCast saves recent playback positions so you can resume later. Videos watched nearly to the end are treated as completed.

items.q: Does FolderCast support subtitles?
items.a: Yes. When supported SRT, VTT, or TTML subtitle files are available alongside a video in the same shared folder, you can select a subtitle or turn subtitles off.

items.q: Can I change the audio track in a video?
items.a: Yes, when the video exposes more than one selectable audio track and your Roku supports it.

items.q: Why does a recognized media file fail to play?
items.a: A recognized extension does not guarantee playback. The video or audio codec, file condition, Roku model, and Roku OS can affect compatibility. Try another compatible file or encoding.

items.q: Is FolderCast free?
items.a: Yes. The free version lets you explore the first 5 subfolders and first 20 playable media files in each folder, in displayed filename order. A subscription unlocks full eligible browsing.

items.q: What does a subscription unlock?
items.a: A FolderCast subscription removes the free browsing limits for eligible folders and media in your shared selections.

items.q: What subscription plans are available?
items.a: Monthly, quarterly, and annual plans may be offered. Available plans and current prices appear in Roku’s purchase experience.

items.q: How do I subscribe or restore a purchase?
items.a: Choose Subscribe in FolderCast and follow Roku’s purchase steps. Existing entitlements are restored from the Roku account after an app restart or reinstall.

items.q: How do I manage or cancel my subscription?
items.a: When premium access is active, select Manage Subscription in FolderCast for a QR code and Roku account instructions. Billing and plan changes are handled by Roku.

items.q: Does FolderCast upload my media to a cloud library?
items.a: No FolderCast cloud media library is required. You explicitly choose which files and folders to share for viewing over your local Wi-Fi.

items.q: Will removing a share or clearing temporary storage delete my originals?
items.a: No. Removing a share stops showing it in FolderCast, and Clear Temporary Storage removes app-managed previews and temporary viewing data. Neither action deletes your original media.

items.q: What happens if my phone or computer disconnects?
items.a: FolderCast shows connection or unavailable-media guidance and can reconnect after brief interruptions. Keep the sharing browser available and both devices on the same Wi-Fi.

items.q: Will my shared folders return after restarting FolderCast?
items.a: FolderCast can restore shared selections after a Roku app restart when the connected browser still has access to those selections. You may need to reconnect or select files again if browser access has been lost.

items.q: Why is my phone unable to connect to the Roku?
items.a: Check that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi, FolderCast is open on Roku, and the browser is using the current address shown on TV. Avoid isolated guest networks and retry the connection.

items.q: Why is a folder empty or a file missing?
items.a: FolderCast lists supported media it can access. Check that the folder contains supported files, that browser access remains available, and that the share has not been removed.

items.q: What does Clear Temporary Storage do?
items.a: It removes FolderCast’s temporary previews and viewing data. Needed previews are recreated during later browsing; original files remain untouched.

items.q: Where can I get help or send feedback?
items.a: Open Support & Feedback in FolderCast and scan the appropriate QR code for support or feedback. The app also includes Help / FAQ and legal information.
